name: Greenwich

licensing.selective: A selective licensing scheme has been in force since 1 October 2022 (for five years) in the Plumstead, Woolwich and Shooters Hill area; sources list the wards slightly differently, so check the address with the council. A larger scheme covering 18 wards, replacing the current one, was consulted on from 21 July to 12 October 2026; no decision had been published when checked.
licensing.additional: Borough-wide additional HMO licensing has applied since 1 January 2024, for smaller shared homes not covered by mandatory HMO licensing.

neighbourhoods.housing: High-rise new-build apartment blocks with concierges, lifts and underground parking.

neighbourhoods.name: Blackheath

neighbourhoods.name: Thamesmead

housing: Greenwich mixes Georgian and Victorian terraces in Greenwich, Blackheath and Plumstead with some of London's largest post-war estates in Woolwich and Thamesmead. Since the 2000s, riverside regeneration at Greenwich Peninsula, the Royal Arsenal and Kidbrooke has added thousands of new-build flats in towers and mid-rise blocks. About a quarter of households rented privately at the 2021 census, and social renting is still common. The council licenses smaller HMOs borough-wide and runs selective licensing in the Plumstead and Woolwich area, with a larger scheme under consultation.
checkinTips: Tower flats on the Peninsula and at the Royal Arsenal: record fob, parking-fob and post-box key counts and photograph the balcony, its drainage and the glass balustrade.
Georgian and Victorian sash windows in Greenwich and Blackheath: photograph cords, catches and any rot or flaking paint on the sills.
Victorian terraces in Plumstead let as shared homes: photograph each room's door lock, smoke alarm and fire door closers, and list which keys open which rooms.
Post-war estate blocks in Woolwich and Thamesmead: note entry-phone, lift and communal-area condition on the day, and photograph any damp in bathrooms and window reveals.
Inter-war houses in Eltham: photograph the garden, fences and any outbuildings, and the condition of the boiler and radiators.
tenantHelp: Private tenants can report disrepair, damp and mould or unsafe conditions to the Royal Borough of Greenwich's private sector housing team, which can inspect and take enforcement action.
